answer: Divergence-challenge fingerprinting.** Each identity must periodically answer a challenge derived from its own prior output history, signed and logged. Clones replaying one script produce identical fingerprints, so any two identities sharing a fingerprint are flagged as one lineage and both are retired. An attacker must therefore give each clone a genuinely divergent history, paying full compute and storage per identity rather than copying a relic once. Detection latency is one epoch; a comet of copied state collapses on first challenge. A marble-sized seed cannot amortize across clones.
